**The content-identity crux — resolved against the Codex remedy, on evidence, by two independent reconcilers.** Codex's central objection across all three lenses was that basename-only coverage never binds a remote file to the current disk file, and that the plan's "content checks need downloads" scope-out is too broad because LFS sha256 is available from Hub metadata. Both the methodology and alternatives reconcilers verified the same split: Codex is RIGHT on the remote half (`hub.list_repo_entries_complete` at hub.py:930-972 already yields `(path, size)` from the paginated `list_repo_tree` walk, whose `RepoFile` entries carry `blob_id` / LFS sha256), and WRONG end-to-end, because the disk half has nothing to compare. `_outroot_disk_entries` (verify_uploads.py:1498-1558) ingests a bare path-per-line `find` capture with no sizes and no digests, and `_file_size_or_unknown` (1486-1495) documents that pod paths cannot be stat'ed from the VM. The decisive evidence is the precedent Codex itself cited: the #2359 git-arm content check (`_match_outroot_files`, 1583-1587) ALREADY degrades to WARN whenever `Path(full).is_file()` is False — i.e. on EVERY row of a pod-side listing — and the terminate gate runs exclusively in that mode (VM verifier against a pod-captured listing). So the remedy resolves to either a new pod-side digest-capture contract (a scope expansion past a Goal naming one file, touching every listing producer plus the upload-verifier recipes) or its own WARN/FAIL fallback firing on ~1,290 of 1,312 rows — which as FAIL makes the gate structurally unable to PASS the overflow-routed runs it exists to verify, recreating the fail-closed incident with extra steps, and as WARN is a blanket annotation with no more binding force than the per-repo coverage counts already specified in §4-B. **The scope-out STANDS; only its stated reason is wrong.**

**Codex methodology MF1 (unconditional default retention) — REJECTED, empirically falsified by this task's own motivating incident.** Codex argued the default stops being evidence once env or flag names another target. #2389 declared the overflow repo via `EPM_2389_DATA_WRITE_REPO` and STILL wrote a file to the canonical repo: `analyzed_tensors`-sibling path `issue2389_q38ce/analysis_tensors/gates/hf_write_canary.json`, which is exactly the one-match arithmetic in §12 A8. The per-issue env convention (the `issue2162_run.py:105` shape) redirects only the writers coded to read it; the canonical repo remains the default target for everything else (canaries, `upload_raw_completions_to_data_repo` defaults, pointer commits). So env/flag naming a repo asserts a write TARGET, never exclusivity, and dropping the default would convert legitimate canonical-resident writes into false FAILs. The remedy also fails to close the hazard it targets: the per-issue env is attempt-invariant, so the dominant retry scenario (prior attempt, same declared repo) keeps the stale-copy channel open under Codex's precedence; it closes only the changed-target-between-attempts variant, and reopens even that whenever a genuine split is declared via repeated flags. And combined with Codex MF2 (which wants the pointer lane removed or opt-in), the #1108 operator-invisible reactive reroute — whose pointer is its ONLY record — would regress to exactly the pre-fix structural blindness.

No run or attempt identity exists anywhere in the system for the verifier to bind against, so "bind the pointer to invocation provenance" has no mechanical anchor without inventing a new write-path contract. What IS real, and independently agreed by the Claude alternatives critic: §4-D defense 1 overstates for this lane — the pointer is ISSUE-grain provenance (some attempt at this prefix rerouted), not run-grain.
